transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-24
Time: 14:00 - 14:52 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Avery Chen (Redwood AE), Marcus Patel (Redwood SE), Leah Ortiz (Skyway PM), Samir Gupta (Skyway Cloud Architect), Nina Park (Skyway Marketplace Ops)

[00:00] Avery Chen: hey everyone, thanks for joining. um quick agenda, we want to align on the marketplace listing requirements, reference arch options for the redwood runtime, and what the joint validation and co-marketing timeline looks like.
[00:12] Leah Ortiz: thanks avery. yes, excited — we got sign-off from marketplace team to evaluate this. nina and samir here will own the technical side.
[00:20] Samir Gupta: hey all. quick context: Skyway marketplace requires an image or AMI plus a terraform module for one-click deploy, or a hosted listing where we redirect to vendor sign-up. we'd prefer an integrated listing with a deployable package for infra teams.
[00:35] Marcus Patel: got it. as background, Redwood supports hosted API + dedicated clusters + private deploy; for marketplace we typically provide a container image and a terraform module that provisions either our dedicated connector or spins up a private deploy in customer VPC depending on the SKU.
[00:50] Nina Park: one immediate Q: how do you handle secrets/KMS and SSO for private deployments? marketplace security folks will want details.
[00:58] Marcus Patel: good q. for private we support customer-managed KMS and HSM integration; we store minimal secrets in vault and use envelope encryption. for SSO we support SAML2/SSO via SSO providers and SCIM for user provisioning — though the transcript from earlier calls said SAML2 sometimes gets transcribed as smal but yeah.
[01:15] Samir Gupta: can you share the exact IAM/service account scopes needed? network-wise we want minimal open ports, prefer PrivateLink or VPC peering.
[01:23] Avery Chen: yes, we'll share a least-privilege permissions doc. network patterns: we can do VPC peering, PrivateLink, or a managed connector that uses outbound-only connections from your VPC to Redwood. PrivateLink is supported but requires extra provisioning on both sides.
[01:36] Leah Ortiz: marketplace listing requires a reference architecture diagram, deployment steps, and an ops runbook. do you have a canonical ref-arch we can reuse?
[01:44] Marcus Patel: we have a few reference architectures — a hosted listing flow, a dedicated-reserved flow for committed customers, and a private VPC/on-prem flow. i'll attach the ref-arch diagram and a simplified terraform module. note: the runtime expects certain kernel optimizations if you're on GPU hosts; we'll call that out in the doc.
[02:05] Samir Gupta: about GPU — Skyway offers both CPU and GPU SKUs. for the GPU path we need to ensure the model and wasm/quantization artifacts are compatible. any recommended quantization or model variants for cost/perf?
[02:17] Marcus Patel: yes, recommend 4-bit quantization profiles for common open models; Redwood Optimize will suggest quantization and batching settings. for marketplace we should list supported model families and recommended profiles in the reference arch.
[02:30] Nina Park: legal and billing Q: how do you want billing mapped? do you expect Skyway to bill for infra and pass tokens to Redwood, or do you want direct billing?
[02:39] Avery Chen: both are possible. common pattern: Skyway bills for infra and a marketplace SKU for Redwood service, and we reconcile usage via reporting. for hosted we usually do direct vendor billing; for marketplace-integrated private deploys we prefer a reseller/marketplace charge mapped to a Redwood account. nina we'll need your marketplace billing contacts.
[02:56] Leah Ortiz: okay, i'll loop in finance. next, validation — marketplace will validate installation and run a functional test. what test artifacts do you provide?
[03:05] Marcus Patel: we provide a validation script, a post-deploy smoke test that runs generation requests, latency checks, and a small eval prompt set to verify quality. we'll also include token-level cost estimates and sample load profiles for your QA team.
[03:20] Samir Gupta: great. on the networking side, we need sample CIDRs and outbound IP ranges for allowlisting. can you provide those?
[03:27] Avery Chen: yes we'll provide a spreadsheet with IP ranges; note that for hosted connectors the ranges are broader, for private deploys we don't require allowlisting except for the initial bootstrap if you choose outbound-only.
[03:40] Nina Park: security docs — SOC2, ISO, penetration test reports — can you share those for marketplace review?
[03:47] Marcus Patel: yes. we'll share SOC 2 Type II summary, ISO attestation, and a redacted pen test report. also audit log format and retention policies — you can configure audit logs to stream to your SIEM via syslog/S3.
[04:00] Leah Ortiz: parity with other vendor listings is important — marketplace team will check for RBAC, SSO, encryption at rest, transit, and auditability.
[04:09] Samir Gupta: another technical nit: what's the recommended KV cache pattern? the docs earlier said KV cash which is fine but we need exact behavior.
[04:16] Marcus Patel: yeah, that was a transcript hiccup — KV cache. our runtime supports persistent KV cache between requests for streaming/completion performance; we'll document TTLs and cache invalidation best practices.
[04:30] Avery Chen: also mentioning co-marketing and joint solution brief — skyway marketplace often wants a 1-pager and a reference architecture visual for the marketplace tile. we can draft a co-branded solution brief once the tech validation passes.
[04:41] Nina Park: timeline wise — marketplace target is late april for go-live if we can finish validation and legal by mid-april. is that realistic?
[04:49] Marcus Patel: technically yes; main blockers are: getting terraform testing in your environment, getting KMS/provisioning set up, and contract/legal sign-off. with the hands-on session and checklist we can hit mid-april for validation.
[05:05] Leah Ortiz: can you walk us through an example flow for a customer who picks the "managed via Skyway" SKU?
[05:12] Marcus Patel: sure. user selects Redwood listing -> Skyway provisions infra SKU (VMs or managed cluster) and attaches marketplace SKU -> terraform module triggers Redwood bootstrap which either registers the runtime to a Redwood tenant in your org or provisions a private deploy in the Skyway VPC -> post-deploy smoke tests run -> billing starts. If you choose hosted, redirect flow sends customer to Redwood sign-up with SSO.
[05:40] Samir Gupta: what about upgrades and rollouts? marketplace wants a safe upgrade path for vendor updates.
[05:47] Avery Chen: we support canary rollouts, pinned model versions, and automatic fallback to previous model variants. for private deploys our operator image includes a bootstrap that can coordinate in-cluster upgrades; we'll add upgrade notes to the runbook.
[06:05] Nina Park: ok great. on co-sell/marketing — skyway requires a basic joint webinar and a case study within 3 months of launch if possible.
[06:14] Leah Ortiz: yep. we can commit to webinar planning once listing is live.
[06:19] Marcus Patel: I'll prepare the sample Terraform and a step-by-step runbook; also a small k8s helm chart for customers who want k8s native deploy.
[06:30] Leah Ortiz: perfect. anything else?
[06:33] Samir Gupta: one more: for private deploy telemetry, can we push anonymized usage metrics to Skyway for billing reconciliation? we need to ensure privacy and compliance.
[06:42] Avery Chen: yes, we can export aggregated usage metrics; we will not share raw prompts. we can schedule a legal check for that data sharing pattern.
[06:51] Nina Park: please include the data-sharing summary in that packet.
[06:55] Avery Chen: noted. OK let's recap next steps — we will send checklist, terraform, and security docs; Skyway will share network diagrams and billing contacts; we'll schedule the hands-on runbook call next week.
[07:10] Leah Ortiz: thanks avery/Marcus — useful sync. we'll aim to have initial full tests by 2026-03-29.
[07:16] Avery Chen: thanks everyone. we'll follow up via email with artifacts.

[END TRANSCRIPT]

Notes: occasional transcription errors (SAML transcribed as smal, KV cache as KV cash). shared artifacts referenced during call: Redwood marketplace checklist (link to be provided), sample terraform module (repo link to be provided), reference architecture diagram (will attach).
